functions.//: The WebAuthn relying party and the photo menu import. Every function is capped with maxInstances in src/config.ts — Blaze bills by invocation, and an uncapped function is what turns a runaway into a bill. Menu import additionally needs the GEMINI_API_KEY secret: firebase functions:secrets:set GEMINI_API_KEY
functions.//predeploy: Calls the TypeScript compiler directly instead of `npm --prefix "$RESOURCE_DIR" run build`, which is what `firebase init` writes. Under npm 11 on Node 26 that form fails inside the Firebase CLI with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'stdin')` and takes the whole deploy with it before a byte is uploaded. The compile itself is fine — the log shows `> tsc` completing, and npm only falls over afterwards, in its own lifecycle wrapper, reaching for a stdin the CLI never gave it. Running the same command by hand in a terminal works, which is what makes it baffling. So npm is cut out of the path: `tsc` is the thing that needs to run, and this runs it. `npm run build` is still there for people, and still does the same job.

hosting.//ignore: `**/.*` used to be here and was the whole reason the association files lived in a non-dotted directory behind a rewrite: it drops every dotted path before upload, so a real .well-known/ never reached Hosting. That workaround does not survive contact with Firebase's own behaviour — see //predeploy below — so the glob is replaced by the two things it was actually there to exclude.
hosting.//predeploy:
Copies the association files into a real `.well-known/` directory, and it is not tidiness — it is the only thing that makes them reachable.

Firebase Hosting SERVES ITS OWN /.well-known/assetlinks.json, generated from the Android apps registered on the project, and it wins over any rewrite. What that generated file said here was worse than nothing: it named `com.example.adsf.revenue` — a leftover app nobody ships — with a fingerprint belonging to neither the debug nor the upload keystore, and it carried only `delegate_permission/common.handle_all_urls`. Passkeys need `delegate_permission/common.get_login_creds`, which was absent, so Android passkeys could not have worked no matter how correct web/well-known/assetlinks.json was.

A real static file at the requested path takes precedence over the generated one. `flutter build web` rebuilds build/web from scratch, so this runs on every deploy rather than being done once by hand.

rewrites.//:
Kept as a fallback, and no longer the mechanism. These two come first because within `rewrites` Hosting applies the first rule whose pattern matches, and the catch-all below would otherwise swallow /.well-known/* along with everything else.

But a rewrite is not what serves these files any more: Hosting generates its own /.well-known/assetlinks.json and that beats any rewrite. See //predeploy above, which copies the real files into build/web/.well-known/ so a static file wins instead. The sources still live in web/well-known/ with no leading dot, because `flutter build web` is what copies them and a dotted directory there is easy to lose track of.

headers.//: Apple fetches this with no file extension and requires application/json. Android's assetlinks.json gets the type from its extension, but is pinned here too so neither depends on Hosting guessing. Both are declared against the /.well-known/ request path, not the rewritten one.

Flutter web output is NOT content-hashed — main.dart.js keeps the same filename every build — so a long immutable max-age would pin browsers to the version they first loaded and no redeploy would reach them. But plain 'no-cache' is worse: Firebase Hosting stops honouring If-None-Match on it and re-sends the whole ~1 MB gzipped bundle on every page load. 'max-age=0, must-revalidate' is the pair that works: revalidate before every use, and get a 304 when the build has not changed.
canvaskit is pinned to the Flutter SDK version, so it may be held longer.

emulators.//: Only Firestore, and only for `test/rules`. The UI is off because the suite is non-interactive and `firebase emulators:exec` should not open a browser in CI; singleProjectMode stops the emulator warning about the test project id not matching the one in .firebaserc.
